items.title: Mollusk family trees play a key role in shaping microbiomes, researchers find
items.summary: A mollusk's microbial community has more to do with its family tree than its address. In other words, the composition of a mollusk's microbiome depends less on the environment in which it lives and more on what species it belongs to, say University of Michigan researchers.

items.title: Examining fraud prevention in federal relief programs
items.summary: SUNY Polytechnic Institute (SUNY Poly) assistant professor of accounting Dr. Katie Matt, in collaboration with Daniel Hebert of Syracuse University, recently published research examining the widespread fraud associated with the federal Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) during the COVID-19 pandemic.

items.summary: NASA will preview two upcoming spacewalks to complete solar array installation and power augmentation of the International Space Station during a news conference at 2 p.m. EDT, Tuesday, Oct. 20, from NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. items.title: Job loss and AI-exposed jobs: Q&A with sociology professor
items.summary: Jennie Brand, a UCLA professor of sociology with an appointment in statistics and data science, is an expert on the socioeconomic effects of job loss, including the long-term economic, psychological, physiological and intergenerational effects.

items.title: Learning reshapes inhibitory synapses differently within the same nerve cell, study suggests
items.summary: Our brain must be able to learn new things without losing previously stored information or the stability of its networks. Researchers at the Leibniz Institute for Neurobiology (LIN) in Magdeburg, together with partners in Bielefeld and Zurich, have investigated how this balance is achieved.

items.summary: Two new research papers shed light on the growing practice of grazing sheep in fields with solar arrays. items.title: Superheavy-element compound reveals weaker-than-expected bond due to relativistic effects
items.summary: An international collaboration led by a research group from GSI/FAIR in Darmstadt, Germany, has achieved the first measurement of the chemical stability of a superheavy element compound.

items.summary: The Arctic is warming four times faster than the rest of the globe, and scientists are racing to understand how that fact affects the region's landscapes and ecosystems. items.title: Employees look to leaders as study finds gap between workplace promises and employee experience
items.summary: A survey of UK employees has revealed that more than half experience a mismatch between what their employer says and what they do in practice, with many looking to leadership behavior when judging an organization's true values.
